subject: English
passage: One challenge faced by researchers such as John Novak and Arjun Tang who study global rural poverty is that different countries use different definitions of what constitutes poverty in rural areas. Many countries define rural poverty using an income threshold per household. However, countries do not all use the same amount; for example, Nepal sets the threshold around $1.90 per person per day, while Romania uses roughly $7.40. Other nations combine income with additional measures, such as access to clean water or availability of basic services. This variation makes it difficult for researchers to compare levels of rural poverty across countries.
prompt: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.A: It is difficult for researchers to compare levels of rural poverty across countries because of the various ways different countries define poverty in rural areas.
choices.B: Although countries use different methods to define rural poverty, researchers consider any household earning less than $7.40 per person per day to be in poverty.
choices.C: Researchers focus on factors other than income when conducting studies on rural poverty in Nepal.
choices.D: Rural poverty is easily compared between countries when they have similar average household incomes.

explanation:
Choice A is the best answer. The passage describes how different countries use different definitions of rural poverty — some use varying income thresholds (like Nepal's $1.90 versus Romania's $7.40), while others combine income with additional measures such as access to clean water. The passage concludes that this variation makes it difficult for researchers to compare levels of rural poverty across countries.

Why C is incorrect:

Choice C is incorrect. Nepal is mentioned only as one example of a country using a low income threshold ($1.90 per person per day). The passage doesn't say anything about what factors researchers focus on when studying rural poverty specifically in Nepal.
